comparison: Perfect agreement on short-term plasticity claims (C12, C13, C75-C85). Both evaluations find the train stimulation data and pharmacological controls convincing evidence for differential plasticity of glutamate and GABA release.

Perfect agreement on frequency-dependent filtering mechanism (C15, C86-C92). Both evaluations accept the current-clamp data demonstrating that co-release modulates granule cell firing in a frequency-dependent manner.

Strong agreement on anatomical evidence for spatially segregated synapses (C9-C11, C66-C74, C112, C114). Both evaluations find the complementary immunofluorescence and EM data compelling, with only minor claim C113 not explicitly addressed by peer reviewers.

Strong agreement on minimal stimulation data (C8, C57-C63). Both evaluations accept the uniquantal analysis as supporting separate vesicle populations, though peer reviewers note this is part of cumulative evidence rather than decisive alone.

Agreement on asynchronous release experiments (C64-C65). Both evaluations accept the Sr2+ data as strengthening the conclusion of independent co-transmission. Peer reviewers consider this part of the broader electrophysiological evidence.

Agreement on paired-pulse ratio data (C4, C40-C44). Both evaluations find the PPR differences and controls for technical confounds convincing. Peer reviewers group this with other differential release properties.
Agreement on differential Ca2+ sensitivity (C5, C45-C47). Both evaluations accept the EGTA-AM data as supporting different Ca2+ sensitivities for glutamate and GABA release.

Agreement on Ca2+ channel pharmacology (C48-C50, C109). Both evaluations accept that both transmitters use N-type Ca2+ channels. Peer reviewers consider this part of the differential release properties evidence.

Agreement on differential presynaptic modulation by baclofen (C6, C51-C53, C110-C111). Both evaluations accept the dose-response data. OpenEval notes C110-C111 are appropriately framed as speculation; peer reviewers focus on the empirical findings.

Agreement on Ca2+ chelator experiments (C7, C54-C56, C99). Both evaluations accept the BAPTA/EGTA data as evidence for tighter coupling for GABA. Peer reviewers consider this part of the comprehensive differential release properties evidence.

Agreement on main conclusion of separate vesicle pools (C14, C65, C96-C98, C100-C101, C121). Both evaluations accept this central conclusion based on converging evidence. Peer Reviewer 2 notes the strength rests on cumulative data rather than any single decisive approach.

Agreement on optogenetic methodology and controls (C41-C43). Both evaluations accept the controls for ChR2 artifacts and fiber volley measurements. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by noting the study is well-designed.

Agreement on uncertainty of functional implications (C124-C126). Both evaluations recognize these are speculative interpretations extending beyond the data. OpenEval notes they require direct validation; peer reviewers find them plausible but not directly tested.

Partial disagreement on ruling out co-packaging (C122). OpenEval rates the acknowledgment of this limitation as SUPPORTED (appropriately cautious), while Reviewer 1 explicitly notes this as a weakness, stating 'thorough elimination of alternative mechanisms would have strengthened the study.'

Divergence on mechanistic speculation (C93-C95, C102-C108). OpenEval finds the discussion appropriately distinguishes speculation from fact. Peer Reviewer 2 raises concerns about unresolved molecular mechanisms (C103, C105), noting 'one is now left with another conundrum' about vesicle sorting and positioning.
OpenEval evaluated background and context claims (C1, C2, C16-C19) establishing the field's knowledge and research gap. Peer reviewers did not explicitly evaluate these introductory claims.
OpenEval evaluated extensive literature review claims (C20-C37) about prior work on co-transmission and SuM projections. Peer reviewers did not explicitly evaluate these background claims.
OpenEval evaluated foundational observations (C3, C38-C39) about SuM terminal anatomy and basic electrophysiology. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these preliminary findings.
OpenEval evaluated integration with prior LTP findings (C127-C128). Peer reviewers did not explicitly evaluate this synthesis with the authors' previous work.
